hazard_indicator: High UTCI Days (ERA5-HEAT; count of days with a Universal Thermal Climate Index above 32 degrees)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the only available index measures human thermal comfort rather than asset-level heat stress, and it is reanalysis-based with no climate projections available (The Climate Data Factory and B-Open et al., 2024).

hazard_granularity: 0.25 degree grid (~28km); 0.11 degree grid for Apparent Temperature Heatwave Days
hazard_indicator: Hot Days, Tropical Nights, Warmest Three Day Period, Climatological Heatwave Days and Apparent Temperature Heatwave Days
coverage_rationale: Full because several dedicated heatwave indices with documented percentile thresholds are provided; the apparent-temperature variant comes from a different input dataset and is therefore not directly comparable with the others (The Climate Data Factory and B-Open et al., 2024).

hazard_indicator: Fire Weather Index and High Fire Danger Days (days with FWI above 30, EFFIS classification)
coverage_rationale: Full because dedicated fire-danger indices are provided; the resolution is finer than that of most other indices in this source, which come from a different input dataset (The Climate Data Factory and B-Open et al., 2024).

hazard_indicator: Extreme Wind Speed Days (days above the 98th percentile of 10m wind speed)
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated wind-extremes index is provided; it is threshold-based and does not identify individual windstorm events (The Climate Data Factory and B-Open et al., 2024).

hazard_indicator: Aridity Actual (ratio of actual evapotranspiration to precipitation)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the only available index describes the climatic water balance and not water stress in the sense of demand relative to available supply (The Climate Data Factory and B-Open et al., 2024).

hazard_indicator: Flood Recurrence (50-year return-period discharge) and River Discharge
coverage_rationale: Full because dedicated river-flooding indices from a hydrological model are provided; the resolution is finer than that of the atmospheric indices in this source, and coverage is limited to riverine flooding (The Climate Data Factory and B-Open et al., 2024).

hazard_indicator: Maximum Consecutive Five-Day Precipitation, Extreme Precipitation Total and Extreme Precipitation Days
coverage_rationale: Full because three dedicated extreme-precipitation indices with documented percentile thresholds are provided (The Climate Data Factory and B-Open et al., 2024).

hazard_granularity: 0.25 degree grid (~28km) for the meteorological indices; 5km grid for the soil-moisture index
hazard_indicator: Meteorological Drought Duration and Magnitude (SPI-3), Consecutive Dry Days and Mean Soil Moisture
coverage_rationale: Full because both meteorological and soil-moisture drought indices are provided; they come from different input datasets, so their resolutions differ and they are not directly comparable (The Climate Data Factory and B-Open et al., 2024).

hazard_indicator: Loss Data module, heat wave category (historical event and damage records)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the hazard appears only in the Loss Data module as historical event and damage records compiled from EM-DAT, media and other secondary sources; the Risk Analysis module provides no modelled forward-looking layer for it (Joint Research Centre / Disaster Risk Management Knowledge Centre, no date).

hazard_indicator: Risk Analysis layer for wildfire, derived from EFFIS data and the wildland-urban interface
coverage_rationale: Full because a modelled hazard layer is provided in the Risk Analysis module and aggregated to administrative units (Joint Research Centre / Disaster Risk Management Knowledge Centre, no date).

hazard_indicator: Loss Data module, windstorm category (historical event and damage records)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the hazard appears only in the Loss Data module as historical event and damage records compiled from EM-DAT, media and other secondary sources; the Risk Analysis module provides no modelled forward-looking layer for it (Joint Research Centre / Disaster Risk Management Knowledge Centre, no date).

hazard_indicator: Risk Analysis layer for river and coastal flood, based on the JRC pan-European flood hazard maps
coverage_rationale: Full because a modelled hazard layer is provided in the Risk Analysis module and aggregated to administrative units; riverine and coastal flooding are covered, pluvial flooding is not (Joint Research Centre / Disaster Risk Management Knowledge Centre, no date).

hazard_indicator: Loss Data module, flash flood category (historical event and damage records)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the hazard appears only in the Loss Data module as historical event and damage records compiled from EM-DAT, media and other secondary sources; the Risk Analysis module provides no modelled forward-looking layer for it (Joint Research Centre / Disaster Risk Management Knowledge Centre, no date).

hazard_indicator: Loss Data module, drought category (historical event and damage records)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the hazard appears only in the Loss Data module as historical event and damage records compiled from EM-DAT, media and other secondary sources; the Risk Analysis module provides no modelled forward-looking layer for it (Joint Research Centre / Disaster Risk Management Knowledge Centre, no date).

hazard_granularity: 200m to 5km grid, finer than the NUTS 2/3 granularity of the other layers
hazard_indicator: Risk Analysis layer for landslide, based on the European Landslide Susceptibility Map ELSUS v2 combined with GPCC precipitation data
coverage_rationale: Full because a modelled susceptibility layer is provided; its resolution is finer than that of the other layers in this source, which are aggregated to administrative units (Joint Research Centre / Disaster Risk Management Knowledge Centre, no date).

hazard_granularity: approximately 8km (ECMWF forecast) to 28km (GEOS-5 forecast); 250m for burnt-area perimeters
hazard_indicator: Fire Weather Index in six danger classes (daily forecast raster) and burnt-area perimeters from the Rapid Damage Assessment
coverage_rationale: Full because dedicated fire-danger and burnt-area products are provided; the forecast grid is coarse relative to Austria, and the index is time-varying, so a static exposure attribute requires an own aggregation choice (Copernicus Emergency Management Service / EFFIS, no date b; Rosadi et al., 2023).

hazard_indicator: No named index; ERA5 soil temperature at four depth levels, as raw variables
coverage_rationale: Partial because no ready-made permafrost index exists in the catalogue; the raw variables are usable only as input to the institution’s own model (Hersbach et al., 2023; ECMWF, 2026).

hazard_indicator: Raw 2m temperature variables (daily minimum, maximum and mean); the derived heatwave indices are published separately as the ECDE indicators dataset
coverage_rationale: Full because the temperature fields are the quantity that defines the hazard; the threshold and the index definition rest with the institution, and ready-made indices are reached through the separate ECDE dataset (ECMWF, 2026).

hazard_indicator: Raw 10m wind-speed variables; the derived Extreme Wind Speed Days index is published separately as part of the ECDE indicators dataset
coverage_rationale: Full because the wind-speed fields are the quantity that defines the hazard; the threshold definition rests with the institution, and the ready-made index is reached through the separate ECDE dataset (ECMWF, 2026).

hazard_indicator: Raw total-precipitation variables; the derived extreme-precipitation indices are published separately as part of the ECDE indicators dataset
coverage_rationale: Full because the precipitation fields are the quantity that defines the hazard; the threshold and the index definition rest with the institution, and ready-made indices are reached through the separate ECDE dataset (ECMWF, 2026).

hazard_indicator: Raw precipitation variables from which SPI-3 can be derived; the soil-moisture component is published separately in the hydrology dataset
coverage_rationale: Partial because the meteorological component must be derived by the institution and the soil-moisture component belongs to a separate ready-made dataset (ECMWF, 2026).

hazard_indicator: No named index; raw precipitation, soil-moisture and wind-speed variables
coverage_rationale: Partial because no erosion index exists in the catalogue; using the source requires independent erosion modelling, for example of the RUSLE type (ECMWF, 2026).

hazard_indicator: Modelled inundation areas HQ30, HQ100 and HQ300 (Hochwasserueberflutungsflaechen)
coverage_rationale: Full because the dataset is the official modelled inundation extent for the 30-, 100- and 300-year events, maintained under the implementation of the Floods Directive (Umweltbundesamt, 2020).

hazard_granularity: Hazard zone polygons, delineated by technical criteria independently of parcel boundaries; can be intersected with parcel or address locations
hazard_indicator: Red and yellow hazard zones for torrent processes (Wildbach)
coverage_rationale: Partial because the plan covers torrent-related flood only, and is mapped only for municipalities with torrent, avalanche or erosion catchments and only within the spatially relevant area (Forsttechnischer Dienst für Wildbach- und Lawinenverbauung, no date).

hazard_granularity: Hazard zone polygons, delineated by technical criteria independently of parcel boundaries; can be intersected with parcel or address locations
hazard_indicator: Red and yellow hazard zones for erosion processes
coverage_rationale: Full because the hazard type is assessed in its own right. Mapped only for municipalities that contain torrent, avalanche or erosion catchments and only within the spatially relevant area, so an unmapped location is ambiguous (Forsttechnischer Dienst für Wildbach- und Lawinenverbauung, no date).

hazard_granularity: Hazard zone polygons, delineated by technical criteria independently of parcel boundaries; can be intersected with parcel or address locations
hazard_indicator: Hazard depiction for rockfall and landslide processes (Steinschlag, Rutschungen)
coverage_rationale: Full because the hazard type is assessed in its own right. Mapped only for municipalities that contain torrent, avalanche or erosion catchments and only within the spatially relevant area, so an unmapped location is ambiguous (Forsttechnischer Dienst für Wildbach- und Lawinenverbauung, no date).

hazard_indicator: Daily wind-gust maps for Austria, provided through the cooperation with GeoSphere Austria
coverage_rationale: Full in the sense that Austria-wide wind information is available, but it describes current conditions rather than a long-term hazard zoning, and its grid is coarser than the parcel-level flood layer (HORA, no date).

hazard_granularity: Parcel/cadastral level; HORA 3D additionally simulates flood depth at building level
hazard_indicator: Gefahrendarstellung Fliessgewaesser: flood hazard zoning for the 30-, 100- and 300-year event, including inundation zones of standing waters
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated Austria-wide flood hazard zoning is provided and can be queried for any address; it is published for first orientation and is not a legally binding hazard zone plan (Bundesministerium für Land- und Forstwirtschaft, Klima- und Umweltschutz, Regionen und Wasserwirtschaft, no date).

hazard_indicator: Landslide susceptibility screening layer, provided through the cooperation with GeoSphere Austria
coverage_rationale: Partial because the layer is an indicative screening product, newer and less mature than the flood layer, and is provided on a grid rather than at parcel level (HORA, no date).

hazard_indicator: Baseline Water Stress, Baseline Water Depletion, Interannual Variability, Seasonal Variability and Groundwater Table Decline
coverage_rationale: Full because several dedicated water-stress indicators are provided, each as a raw value, a score on a scale from 0 to 5 and a category label; they are modelled with PCR-GLOBWB 2 and describe demand relative to available supply (World Resources Institute, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Riverine Flood Risk and Coastal Flood Risk indicators
coverage_rationale: Full because dedicated flood indicators are provided in their own right rather than inferred from the water-stress indicators; they express expected annual affected population and assets, not inundation depth (World Resources Institute, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Drought Risk indicator
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated drought indicator is provided; it combines hazard, exposure and vulnerability into a risk score rather than describing the meteorological drought itself (World Resources Institute, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Heat Stress risk category of Climate on Demand (category score and sub-category scores on a 0 to 100 scale); the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because heat stress is one of the named risk categories scored per facility (Moody's ESG Solutions, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Wildfires risk category of Climate on Demand (category score and sub-category scores on a 0 to 100 scale); the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because wildfires are one of the named risk categories scored per facility (Moody's ESG Solutions, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Water Stress risk category of Climate on Demand (category score and sub-category scores on a 0 to 100 scale); the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because water stress is one of the named risk categories scored per facility (Moody's ESG Solutions, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Floods risk category of Climate on Demand (category score and sub-category scores on a 0 to 100 scale); the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because floods are one of the named risk categories scored per facility (Moody's ESG Solutions, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Heat Stress Index of the Climate Change Edition
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated heat-stress index is named among the eight climate hazard scores, provided per location for current conditions and for four projection years and scenarios (Munich Re, Risk Management Partners, no date c).

hazard_indicator: No separately named acute heat product; covered within the Heat Stress Index
coverage_rationale: Partial because only a chronic heat-stress index is named; whether acute heatwave events are distinguished is not stated in the product description (Munich Re, Risk Management Partners, no date c).

hazard_indicator: Wildfire peril of the Natural Hazards Edition and the Fire Weather Stress Index of the Climate Change Edition
coverage_rationale: Full because wildfire is scored in both editions, as a current hazard and as a forward-looking index (Munich Re, Risk Management Partners, no date c).

hazard_indicator: Extratropical Storm and Tropical Cyclone perils of the Natural Hazards Edition
coverage_rationale: Full because extratropical storm is scored as a named peril, which is the relevant process for Austria (Munich Re, Risk Management Partners, no date c).

hazard_indicator: No dedicated index; covered indirectly through the Drought Stress Index
coverage_rationale: Partial because water stress is not among the eight named climate hazard scores and is only approximated by the drought index (Munich Re, Risk Management Partners, no date c).

hazard_indicator: River Flood and Storm Surge perils of the Natural Hazards Edition, plus the River Flood climate hazard score
coverage_rationale: Full because river flood is scored as a named peril in both editions (Munich Re, Risk Management Partners, no date c).

hazard_indicator: Precipitation Stress Index of the Climate Change Edition
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated precipitation index is named among the eight climate hazard scores; the Natural Hazards Edition additionally scores flash flood as a separate peril (Munich Re, Risk Management Partners, no date c).

hazard_indicator: Drought Stress Index of the Climate Change Edition
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated drought index is named among the eight climate hazard scores (Munich Re, Risk Management Partners, no date c).

hazard_indicator: Landslide peril of the Natural Hazards Edition
coverage_rationale: Full because landslide is one of the fifteen named hazard scores of the Natural Hazards Edition (Munich Re, Risk Management Partners, no date c).

hazard_indicator: Extreme heat hazard class
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated hazard class based on probabilistic heat data is provided; the reported value is the highest class within the administrative unit (GFDRR, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Wildfire hazard class
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated hazard class is provided; the reported value is the highest class within the administrative unit (GFDRR, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Cyclone hazard class
coverage_rationale: Partial because the hazard model and terminology are tropical-cyclone-oriented; applicability to European extratropical windstorms could not be confirmed from the documentation (GFDRR, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Water scarcity hazard class, based on a water stress index expressed as water availability per person per year
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated hazard class describing water availability relative to population is provided (GFDRR, no date a).

hazard_indicator: River flood, urban flood and coastal flood hazard classes
coverage_rationale: Full because three dedicated flood hazard classes are provided; the reported value is the highest class within the administrative unit, not the hazard at a specific location (GFDRR, no date a).

hazard_indicator: No dedicated class; drought is only indirectly inferable from the water scarcity hazard class
coverage_rationale: Partial because drought is not covered as a distinct event-based hazard, only through the chronic water scarcity class (GFDRR, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Landslide hazard class, derived from the Global Landslide Hazard Map (Arup for World Bank/GFDRR)
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated landslide dataset underlies the classification; the value is delivered as a district-level class rather than as the underlying grid (World Bank and Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery et al., no date).

hazard_indicator: No named index; daily precipitation fields (RR) since 1961
coverage_rationale: Full because the daily fields at 1 km resolution allow a heavy-precipitation index to be derived directly; the source supplies the variable, the threshold definition rests with the institution (GeoSphere Austria, no date a).

hazard_indicator: No named index; daily minimum, maximum and mean temperature fields (TN, TX, TM, TM24) since 1961
coverage_rationale: Full because the daily fields at 1 km resolution allow a heatwave index to be derived directly; the source supplies the variables, the threshold definition rests with the institution (GeoSphere Austria, no date a).

hazard_indicator: No named index; daily precipitation and temperature fields
coverage_rationale: Partial because the fields support only a basic dryness proxy; no drought index is part of this dataset, and the dedicated index is published separately as WINFORE (GeoSphere Austria, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) at 30-, 90- and 365-day aggregation
coverage_rationale: Full because a dedicated, purpose-built drought index is provided at national 1 km resolution (GeoSphere Austria, no date b).

hazard_indicator: Reference evapotranspiration (ET0) and the climatic water balance underlying the SPEI
coverage_rationale: Partial because the climatic water balance is oriented towards drought and dryness, not towards water stress in the sense of demand relative to available supply (GeoSphere Austria, no date b).

hazard_indicator: Fluvial, pluvial and coastal flood perils of Spectra; the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because all three flood processes are named individually and modelled at street level (Climate X Ltd, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Landslide peril of Spectra; the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because landslide is named individually among the modelled perils (Climate X Ltd, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Windstorm peril of Spectra; the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because a windstorm peril is named among the modelled perils (Climate X Ltd, no date a).

hazard_indicator: No separately named acute heat product; covered within the extreme heat peril; the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Partial because only the chronic heat metric is named; whether acute heatwave events are distinguished could not be established from the public documentation (Climate X Ltd, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Extreme heat peril of Spectra; the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because extreme heat is named individually among the modelled perils (Climate X Ltd, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Combined drought / water stress peril of Spectra
coverage_rationale: Partial because drought is named among the eleven physical risks but is combined with water stress into a single peril, so the two are not reported separately (Climate X Ltd, no date b).

hazard_indicator: Combined drought / water stress peril of Spectra
coverage_rationale: Partial because water stress is named among the eleven physical risks but is combined with drought into a single peril, so the two are not reported separately (Climate X Ltd, no date b).

hazard_indicator: Wildfire peril of Spectra; the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because wildfire is named among the modelled perils (Climate X Ltd, no date a).

hazard_indicator: Flood perils of ClimateScore Global (fluvial, pluvial and coastal); the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because flood is named individually among the modelled perils and resolved at asset level (Jupiter Intelligence, Inc., no date a).

hazard_indicator: Wind peril of ClimateScore Global; the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because wind is named individually among the modelled perils (Jupiter Intelligence, Inc., no date a).

hazard_indicator: Extreme and chronic precipitation perils of ClimateScore Global
coverage_rationale: Full because extreme and prolonged precipitation are named among the modelled perils (Jupiter Intelligence, Inc., no date b).

hazard_indicator: Heat peril of ClimateScore Global; the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because heat is named individually among the modelled perils (Jupiter Intelligence, Inc., no date a).

hazard_indicator: No separately named chronic heat-stress product; covered within the heat peril; the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Partial because only a general heat peril is named; whether it distinguishes chronic heat stress from acute heatwave events could not be established from the public documentation (Jupiter Intelligence, Inc., no date a).

hazard_indicator: Drought peril of ClimateScore Global; the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because drought is named individually among the modelled perils (Jupiter Intelligence, Inc., no date a).

hazard_indicator: Water stress peril of ClimateScore Global
coverage_rationale: Full because water stress is named as a separate peril, added to the platform alongside extreme cold (Jupiter Intelligence, Inc., no date b).

hazard_indicator: Wildfire peril of ClimateScore Global; the underlying index and model are not publicly documented
coverage_rationale: Full because wildfire is named individually among the modelled perils (Jupiter Intelligence, Inc., no date a).

hazard_indicator: Flood Recurrence and River Discharge from the SIS Operational Water Service hydrology dataset
coverage_rationale: Full because the indices are published as a ready-made dataset that can be requested directly; coverage is limited to riverine flooding (Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute et al., no date).

hazard_indicator: High UTCI Days from the ERA5-HEAT dataset (hourly UTCI and mean radiant temperature, 1940 to present)
coverage_rationale: Full because a peer-reviewed thermal-stress dataset is published in its own right; it is reanalysis-based only, with no projections available (Di Napoli et al., 2021).

hazard_indicator: Mean Soil Moisture from the SIS Operational Water Service hydrology dataset
coverage_rationale: Full for the soil-moisture component, which is published as a ready-made indicator; the meteorological SPI-3 component is not part of this dataset and must be derived from raw variables (Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute et al., no date).

hazard_indicator: Aridity Actual from the SIS Operational Water Service hydrology dataset
coverage_rationale: Full in the sense that a ready-made indicator is published; as with Climate-ADAPT it describes the climatic water balance rather than demand relative to supply (Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute et al., no date).
